name: ls
summary: List a directory or describe a single file.

params.name: path
params.description: Directory or file to list. Defaults to the working directory; supports a leading ~.

params.name: all
params.description: Include entries starting with a dot (passes -A).

params.name: long
params.description: Long format with permissions, owner, size, and mtime (passes -l).

params.name: human_readable
params.description: Human-readable sizes when combined with long (passes -h).

params.name: recursive
params.description: Recursively list subdirectories (passes -R). Use sparingly on deep trees.

params.name: sort_by_size
params.description: Sort by file size, largest first (passes -S).

params.name: sort_by_time
params.description: Sort by modification time, newest first (passes -t).

name: pwd
summary: Show the server's current working directory.

name: largest_files
summary: List the largest files under a directory, ranked by size. Returns only the top N (default 10), so use this instead of find for 'biggest files' questions.

params.name: dir
params.description: Directory to scan recursively. Defaults to the working directory; supports a leading ~.

params.name: count
params.description: How many of the largest files to return (default 10, maximum 100).

name: file
summary: Identify the type of one or more files (e.g. "PNG image data", "ASCII text").

params.name: paths
params.description: One or more files to identify; supports a leading ~.

name: stat
summary: Show detailed metadata (size, mtime, permissions, owner) for one or more paths.

params.name: paths
params.description: One or more paths to stat; supports a leading ~.

name: wc
summary: Count lines, words, characters, or bytes in one or more files. Omit paths to count piped input as the non-first stage of a pipeline.

params.name: lines
params.description: Count lines (passes -l).

params.name: words
params.description: Count words (passes -w).

params.name: bytes
params.description: Count bytes (passes -c).

params.name: chars
params.description: Count characters (passes -m).

params.name: paths
params.description: Files to count; supports a leading ~. Required when calling wc directly; omit only when this is a non-first pipeline stage.

name: du
summary: Report disk usage for one or more paths. Set max_depth to 0 for just a per-argument total.

params.name: human_readable
params.description: Human-readable sizes like 1.2K, 47M, 3G (passes -h).

params.name: total
params.description: Produce a grand total across all arguments (passes -c).

params.name: max_depth
params.description: Report entries at most N directory levels deep (passes -d N). Use 0 to get only the total of each argument (the summary view).

params.name: paths
params.description: Directories or files to measure; supports a leading ~.

name: find
summary: Locate files by name, extension, type, or depth under a directory.

params.name: path
params.description: Root directory to search under; supports a leading ~.

params.name: name_pattern
params.description: Glob to match the base file name, e.g. *.png (passes -name).

params.name: iname_pattern
params.description: Case-insensitive variant of name_pattern (passes -iname).

params.name: type
params.description: Restrict to f (regular file), d (directory), or l (symlink).

params.name: max_depth
params.description: Maximum directory depth to descend (passes -maxdepth).

params.name: min_depth
params.description: Minimum directory depth before matching begins (passes -mindepth).

params.name: extensions
params.description: File extensions without the leading dot, e.g. ["png","jpg"]. OR-combined and matched case-insensitively.

name: grep
summary: Search files or directories for a regular expression. Binary files are skipped. Omit paths to search piped input as the non-first stage of a pipeline.

params.name: pattern
params.description: Regular expression to search for.

params.name: paths
params.description: Files or directories to search; supports a leading ~. Required when calling grep directly; omit only when this is a non-first pipeline stage.

params.name: recursive
params.description: Recurse into directories (passes -r).

params.name: ignore_case
params.description: Case-insensitive match (passes -i).

params.name: line_numbers
params.description: Prefix matches with line numbers (passes -n). On by default unless a summary mode (files_with_matches or count) is selected.

params.name: files_with_matches
params.description: List only the names of files containing matches (passes -l).

params.name: count
params.description: Print only a count of matching lines per file (passes -c).

params.name: max_count
params.description: Stop after this many matches per file (passes -m).

params.name: context
params.description: Print N lines of leading and trailing context around each match (passes -C N).

params.name: include
params.description: Restrict a recursive search to files matching this glob (passes --include=).

name: sort
summary: Sort lines of text. Rarely useful standalone (it needs explicit files); its real purpose is ranking another stage's output as part of a pipeline, e.g. ranking find or du results.

params.name: numeric
params.description: Sort numerically rather than lexicographically (passes -n).

params.name: human_numeric
params.description: Sort by human-readable numeric value, understanding suffixes like 1K, 2M, 3G (passes -h). Use this to rank du -h output by size.

params.name: reverse
params.description: Reverse the sort order, e.g. largest first when combined with numeric or human_numeric (passes -r).

params.name: unique
params.description: Output only the first of each set of equal lines (passes -u).

params.name: key
params.description: Sort key field specification, e.g. "2,2" to sort by the second whitespace-separated field (passes -k).

params.name: paths
params.description: Files to sort; supports a leading ~. Required when calling sort directly; omit only when this is a non-first pipeline stage, in which case it sorts the previous stage's output.

name: head
summary: Show the first N lines (or bytes) of text. Rarely useful standalone; its real purpose is trimming a ranked or filtered pipeline result down to a top-N answer.

params.name: count
params.description: Number of lines to print (passes -n). Defaults to 10 if neither count nor bytes is set.

params.name: bytes
params.description: Number of bytes to print instead of lines (passes -c). Set at most one of count/bytes.

params.name: paths
params.description: Files to read; supports a leading ~. Required when calling head directly; omit only when this is a non-first pipeline stage, in which case it trims the previous stage's output.

name: mkdir
summary: Create a new directory. Reversible: undo removes the created directory (only if still empty).

params.name: path
params.description: Directory to create; supports a leading ~. The parent must already exist and the target must not already exist.

name: move
summary: Move (or rename) a file or directory. Reversible: undo moves it back to its original location.

params.name: source
params.description: Existing file or directory to move; supports a leading ~. Must not begin with '-' (prefix with ./ if needed).

params.name: destination
params.description: Target path; supports a leading ~. If it is an existing directory the source is placed inside it under its own name; otherwise it is the new path. The computed destination must not already exist (no overwrite).

name: copy
summary: Copy a file or directory (recursive). Reversible: undo moves the new copy to the Trash.

params.name: source
params.description: Existing file or directory to copy; supports a leading ~. Must not begin with '-' (prefix with ./ if needed).

params.name: destination
params.description: Target path; supports a leading ~. If it is an existing directory the copy is placed inside it under the source's name; otherwise it is the new path. The computed destination must not already exist (no overwrite).

name: remove
summary: Delete a file or directory by moving it to the Trash (never a hard delete). Reversible: undo restores it from the Trash.

params.name: path
params.description: Existing file or directory to send to the Trash; supports a leading ~. Must not begin with '-' (prefix with ./ if needed).
